decisions.selected: Retain ownership of issues assigned to a relevant recent contributor.
decisions.rationale: The adoption workflow explicitly directs assignment to a relevant contributor; it does not require issue completion.

decisions.selected: Issues with github-actions[bot] assignment events in the one-day run window.
decisions.rationale: Assignment events identify the concrete issues selected by a run without relying on traces or comments.

decisions.selected: Reconstruct the complete batch from issue events when case and event are null.
decisions.rationale: Issue-event history is same-repository evidence available for historical runs and preserves duplicate run keys.

decisions.selected: Issue assignment and unassignment events only.
decisions.rationale: Events directly establish whether assigned ownership remains, while excluded sources only describe activity or judgment.
A one-day horizon aligns with the daily schedule and gives a stable observation window for the assignment action.

decisions.selected: Retained assignments divided by assigned issues.
decisions.rationale: The proportion directly measures sustained ownership for the batch and is bounded in [0,1].
No comparable pre-adoption automated run subject and assignment window exists to score under the same contract.

decisions.selected: Assignment batch capacity is reported separately.
alternatives: Include batch size in the primary value
decisions.rationale: Batch size is context and does not establish retained ownership.

uncertainties.description: Retained assignment demonstrates ownership continuity but cannot establish contributor relevance or future work.
Historical reconstruction is unavailable when GitHub search or issue-event pagination is incomplete.
The daily cadence supports a one-day observation horizon, but it does not prove a causal effect.
